claims.statement: The build pipeline has two modes: `npm run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) produces a static SPA in `dist/` with no Electron output, and `npm run build:electron` (`cross-env ELECTRON=1 npm run build && electron-builder --publish never`) activates the Electron main/preload build and packages the desktop app. The `vite-plugin-electron` integration is gated on `ELECTRON=1`; without it `vite` builds only the renderer.

The Electron preload script is emitted as CommonJS with a `.cjs` extension because the package is `type: module`; a `.js`/`.mjs` preload would be treated as ESM while Electron loads preload scripts as CommonJS. Vite's rollup output is forced to `format: cjs` with `entryFileNames: '[name].cjs'`.

`scripts/ci.sh` is the provider-agnostic single source of truth for CI, running from the repo root under `set -euo pipefail` in order: install (`npm ci` or `npm install`, skippable via `SKIP_INSTALL=1`), typecheck (`npm run typecheck`), wiki-link check (`npm run check:wiki`), tests (`npm test`), and the static SPA build (`npm run build`).

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `scripts/ci.sh` on `ubuntu-latest` (Node 24) on push to `main` and on every pull request, but deliberately does not add a push-on-every-branch trigger to avoid double-building PR branches. A concurrency group keyed on `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true` keeps only the newest run per ref.

The integration and e2e tests live in a reusable workflow `integration-tests.yml` (`workflow_call`/`workflow_dispatch`) separate from per-PR CI. The `integration-test` job runs the jsdom-based `test:integration` suite (which mocks the platform seam), while the `e2e-test` job runs a real packaged-Electron Playwright smoke test (`test:e2e`) under `xvfb-run -a` because Electron opens a real native window on Linux.

The default vitest config excludes the slow integration suite (`*.integration.test.*`) so `npm test` is a fast per-PR unit gate; the integration suite runs separately via `test:integration` with its own `vitest.integration.config.ts`.

`release.yml` triggers on a published GitHub Release (and `workflow_dispatch` dry runs), gates its build job on the reusable `integration-tests.yml` via `uses:`, and runs a per-OS matrix (`fail-fast: false`): macOS produces dmg (arm64+x64), Windows nsis, Linux AppImage, each via `scripts/build-electron.sh`.

`release.yml` always uploads artifacts to the workflow run (`if-no-files-found: error`) so manual `workflow_dispatch` builds are downloadable, but attaches them to the release via `softprops/action-gh-release` only when `github.event_name == 'release'`. Windows uploads `*.exe`, `*.exe.blockmap`, `latest.yml`, `latest.yml.sig`; Linux uploads `*.AppImage`, `latest-linux.yml`, `latest-linux.yml.sig`; macOS uploads `*.dmg` with no feed.

`scripts/build-electron.sh` mirrors `ci.sh`: runs from the repo root, optionally installs deps (`SKIP_INSTALL=1` to skip), runs `npm run build:electron`, and lists `./release/`. electron-builder auto-detects the host OS and emits the matching target (dmg/nsis/AppImage) into `./release/`.

Because there is no purchased Authenticode/Apple certificate, `scripts/sign-release.cjs` independently signs the electron-updater feed file (`latest.yml`/`latest-linux.yml`) with an Ed25519 private key from the `RELEASE_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` secret, writing `<path>.sig` (base64). It runs only on Windows/Linux (macOS has no feed).

The matching release-signing public key is baked into the app at build time (`RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY_B64` in `src/model/updateSignature.ts`) and never fetched from the release channel, so a compromised release cannot republish a matching fake key. `verifyReleaseSignature` returns false for any malformed key, malformed signature, or genuine mismatch.

At runtime `electron/main.ts`'s `verifyUpdateFeed` fetches the feed file and its `.sig` directly from the release download URL and only proceeds to `autoUpdater.downloadUpdate()` after `verifyReleaseSignature` passes, chaining trust: the project's signature covers the feed file and electron-updater's sha512 check then covers the installer against the now-trusted feed. `autoDownload` and `autoInstallOnAppQuit` are both false, so downloads require an explicit `update:download` and installs require `update:install`.

Self-update is Windows/Linux only. macOS is excluded because electron-updater's Squirrel.Mac path needs a real Apple Developer ID signature and notarization to pass Gatekeeper, which the project does not have; mac keeps a check-only update banner instead.

The installers themselves are unsigned by Apple/Microsoft. On macOS the `afterPack` hook (`scripts/afterPack.cjs`) applies a free ad-hoc signature (`codesign --force --deep --sign -`) when no `CSC_LINK`/`CSC_NAME` certificate is configured, downgrading the quarantine 'damaged' dead-end to an 'unidentified developer' prompt the user can bypass; if a real certificate is configured the hook returns early so it does not clobber a proper signature.

The electron-builder `build` config in `package.json` sets appId `io.github.gram21.sailor`, productName `SaiLoR`, asar true, compression maximum, electronLanguages `en-US`, a files list (dist, dist-electron, build/icon.png, excluding maps and node_modules), output dir `release`, the `afterPack` hook, a GitHub publish provider (owner Gram21/repo SaiLoR), and platform targets: macOS dmg arm64+x64, Windows nsis, Linux AppImage, each with a `${productName}-${version}-<os>-${arch}.${ext}` artifactName.
`package.json` declares `allowScripts: { "esbuild@0.25.12": true }`, permitting only esbuild's install script to run while blocking all other post-install scripts.

`Dockerfile.electron` is a build image for the Linux Electron installer using a Debian base (`node:22-bookworm`, not Alpine) because electron-builder needs glibc; it installs `ca-certificates` and `fakeroot`, runs `npm ci`, and defaults to `npm run build:electron`, producing Linux AppImage installers into `/app/release`. Windows/macOS installers must be built on their native OS (Windows can be cross-built by swapping the base for `electronuserland/builder:wine`).

`docker-compose.dev.yml` bind-mounts the source at `.:/app` (with a named `/app/node_modules`) so the image only carries toolchain + dependencies; the standard invocation is `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml run --rm electron`, and the `CMD` can be overridden for other tasks like `npm run build` or `npm test`.

`openwiki.yml` is the scheduled weekly (Monday 06:00 UTC) OpenWiki refresh: it stops early unless `main` has relevant (non-`openwiki/**`) commits in the last 7 days, installs `openwiki` plus `mermaid`/`jsdom` for real mermaid-fence validation, runs `openwiki --update --print`, discards the CLI's self-scaffolded `openwiki-update.yml` and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` snippets, and opens a PR scoped to `openwiki`.

The static SPA build remains the per-PR type-check/build gate, but the browser deployment itself is discontinued: the non-Electron runtime uses `createUnsupportedAdapter`, which refuses every action and surfaces a 'SaiLoR for the web is discontinued — use the desktop app.' notice instead of project-opening UI, while the `PlatformAdapter` seam is kept even though Electron is the only real implementation.

Exactly three wiki-related workflows exist in `.github/workflows/` (`openwiki.yml`, `wiki-publish.yml`, `wiki-import.yml`). The `openwiki` CLI unconditionally re-scaffolds its own recurrence setup on every run — rewriting `.github/workflows/openwiki-update.yml` with its default schedule and refreshing `OPENWIKI:START/END` snippets in `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` — so `openwiki.yml` explicitly deletes/discards all of it on every run as an explicit, independent guarantee (beyond the PR's `add-paths: openwiki` filter), and the repo deliberately carries only the customized `openwiki.yml`.

`wiki-publish.yml` (*Publish openwiki → Wiki*) triggers on push to `main` under `openwiki/**`, `user-guide/**`, `.github/wiki-assets/**`, or the workflow file (plus `workflow_dispatch`), and stages a combined wiki layout: `Home.md` copied verbatim from `.github/wiki-assets/Home.md` (first line `<!-- wiki-sync:auto-home -->`), `openwiki/Home.md` staged as `Development.md` (with a synthesized fallback `Development.md` carrying the same marker when `openwiki/` provides none), flat top-level `openwiki/*.md` (skipping `index.md`/`INSTRUCTIONS.md` as generator bookkeeping), `SUBWIKI_PAGES` flattening of `openwiki/{concepts,operations,workflows}/*.md` to `Concepts-*`/`Operations-*`/`Workflows-*` names, `GUIDE_PAGES` flattening of `user-guide/*.md` to `User-Guide`/`Guide-*`, `screenshots/` flattened alongside, and `_Sidebar.md`/`_Footer.md` assembled from the wiki-assets chrome. It strips OKF YAML frontmatter (gollum cannot render it), rewrites cross-links to the wiki's extensionless flat URLs on the staged copies only, and `rsync --delete` replaces the wiki (not a merge), committing as `github-actions[bot]` with a `[wiki-sync]` marker only when something actually changed.

`wiki-import.yml` (*Import Wiki → openwiki*) is the reverse direction, triggering on `gollum` (a wiki page create/update) and `workflow_dispatch`. It clones the wiki and undoes the publish mapping: a `Home.md` still carrying the `wiki-sync:auto-home` marker is dropped as a no-op while a human-replaced Home becomes the new `.github/wiki-assets/Home.md` template; `Development.md` → `openwiki/Home.md`; the marked "User Guide" fragments are extracted into `.github/wiki-assets/Sidebar-user-guide.md`/`Footer-user-guide.md` and the remainders become the plain developer-docs `Sidebar.md`/`Footer.md` assets (dev-docs link rewritten back to `Home`); `SUBWIKI_PAGES`/`GUIDE_PAGES` reverse renames run dir-aware per-page link fixups before the generic rewrite and move each page back under `openwiki/{concepts,operations,workflows}/` and `user-guide/`; `screenshots/` is restored only if the wiki actually has it (a temporarily missing folder is never mistaken for a deletion); and the remaining `*.md` are rsynced into `openwiki/` preserving `.last-update.json`, committing to `main` as `github-actions[bot]` with a `[wiki-sync]` marker.

`.github/wiki-assets/` is the publish-side chrome source. `Sidebar.md`/`Footer.md` are the developer-docs navigation, deliberately kept out of `openwiki/` so `scripts/check-wiki-links.js` can validate them as `extraPages` against the real openwiki page set (they link into it and the orphan check runs against `Sidebar.md`). `Sidebar-user-guide.md`/`Footer-user-guide.md` are "User Guide" fragments wrapped in `<!-- wiki-sync:user-guide-sidebar|footer:start/end -->` marker pairs — invisible HTML comments on the wiki — that `wiki-import.yml` lifts back out on round-trip. The sidebar leads with the user guide (fragment first, developer nav after, matching Home.md); the footer appends the fragment last since a footer reads along one line rather than top-to-bottom. Publish rewrites `Sidebar.md`'s own `[SaiLoR — Developer Documentation](Home)` link to `Development` on the staged copy only (Home.md is staged as Development.md), matched on exact link text so the fragment's `[🏠 Wiki home](Home)` keeps pointing at the real Home page — the asset file itself keeps saying `Home`, the real openwiki page name, so it keeps validating.

The wiki `Home.md` carries the `<!-- wiki-sync:auto-home -->` marker as a round-trip contract: publish always stages `.github/wiki-assets/Home.md` verbatim and synthesizes a fallback `Development.md` with the same marker when `openwiki/` has no `Home.md` (so import can recognize it as ours rather than a human's page), while import drops a still-marked `Home.md` as a no-op and treats an unmarked Home as a human's wholesale replacement that becomes the new asset template — never `openwiki/Home.md`, which is `Development.md` now.

All publish-side transforms — OKF frontmatter stripping, extensionless cross-link rewrites (bare `name.md` → flat alias; dir-aware relative fixes for `SUBWIKI_PAGES` pages: same-subsection siblings stay bare, walk-ups become `../name.md`; `user-guide/README.md`'s `../README.md`/`../LICENSE` links → absolute GitHub URLs preserving `#heading` anchors; `Home` → `Development` in the staged sidebar) — run on the staged copies only; the repo's own `openwiki/`, `user-guide/`, and `.github/wiki-assets/` files keep the forms that are correct for repo browsing and for `scripts/check-wiki-links.js` validation.

`scripts/check-wiki-links.js` (`npm run check:wiki`, step 3 of `scripts/ci.sh`) is the wiki's build step over `openwiki/` and `user-guide/`, enforcing four rules: (1) every internal link resolves to a page (both bare `name` and `name.md` forms accepted); (2) every `#anchor` matches GitHub's own anchor-slug rules, reproduced rather than approximated, including the `-1`/`-2` suffixes GitHub appends to duplicate headings in document order; (3) every link/image outside the bare-page-name form — a path leaving the directory or an image — resolves to a real file on disk, with screenshots scanned via a separate `` pass (they are embedded as HTML for the `width=` attribute, so the markdown-link scan never sees them); and (4) every page is reachable from the directory's hand-maintained table of contents — `.github/wiki-assets/Sidebar.md` for `openwiki/`, the "Guide contents" table of `user-guide/README.md` for the user guide — so a new page cannot be trivially left orphaned.

`index.md` (OKF's own directory listing) and `INSTRUCTIONS.md` (the brief handed to the generator) are deliberately exempt from the orphan check — generator bookkeeping that is never published to the wiki. Each `SUBWIKI_PAGES` page is registered in the checker twice (under its flat alias, what `Sidebar.md` actually links to, and under its real basename so same-page `#anchor` links and bare sibling cross-references resolve, the basename exempted since only the flat alias is a reachable wiki page). The `SUBWIKI_PAGES` table is hand-duplicated across `wiki-publish.yml`, `wiki-import.yml`, and `check-wiki-links.js`, with `.github/wiki-assets/Sidebar.md` linking the flat names — so adding, moving, or renaming an openwiki subsection page requires updating all four in the same change. The duplication is the price of the flattening, which exists because GitHub's hosted wiki cannot serve pages that live in subdirectories.

Publish and import would otherwise form an infinite loop (publish→gollum→import→main push→publish). Three independent layers prevent it: both share a `concurrency: group: wiki-sync` with `cancel-in-progress: false` so they never run concurrently; `wiki-publish.yml` skips commits whose message contains `[wiki-sync]`; and `wiki-import.yml` skips when `github.event.sender.login == 'github-actions[bot]'`, so each direction only reacts to human-originated changes on the other side.
